newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-LAWRENCE BACK AFTER FIVE-YEAR INJURY ABSENCE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LAWRENCE BACK AFTER FIVE-YEAR INJURY ABSENCE.

text.p: Former England fast bowler David Lawrence marked his return to first-class cricket after a five-year injury absence with a wicket in his seventh over on Wednesday.
Lawrence, who shattered his left kneecap while bowling on the final day of England's 1992 test series in New Zealand, made his comeback for Gloucestershire against Hampshire at Bristol.
A late choice for the four-day county championship match, the 33-year-old paceman had to come through a fitness test on niggling muscle pulls which had been delaying his return.
Lawrence had Hampshire opener Jason Laney caught in the deep as captain Mark Alleyne carefully nursed him with two bursts of four overs.
In a respectable first spell he altered the length of his run-up regularly, but when he switched ends, he generated something like his old pace from what was approaching his more familiar run.
Lawrence ended the first day with one for 70 from 15 overs as Hampshire scored 221 for six, ex-England batsman Robin Smith (52) being top scorer.
Middlesex batsman Mark Ramprakash, who has failed to fulfill his potential at test level, gave England's selectors a sparkling reminder of his ability with 145 against Sussex at Lord's.
Ramprakash, whose 19 tests have produced 533 runs at an average of 16.65, spurred his county to 337 for five at the close on the first day.
He made his 145 from 247 deliveries, hitting 18 fours and a six and giving Middlesex control through his fifth wicket partnership of 136 with Keith Brown, who hit an unbeaten 72.
Northamptonshire's new overseas signing, Pakistan paceman Mohammad Akram, has set himself a target of 100 wickets this season.
Akram, who has played in six tests, outlined his objective as his adopted county scored 126 for four against Somerset on the rain-curtailed first day at Northampton.
He said: "If I could take 100 wickets it would be a successful season for me but you can't predict anything in cricket.
"I have had no problems so far. I didn't play in the two one-day matches this week but it was simply a case of taking a rest with a slight strain which is now getting better."
Durham captain and former Australian batsman David Boon pulled off a masterstroke by asking veteran Alan Walker to lead his side's attack against Nottinghamshire at Hartlepool.
The 34-year-old medium pacer responded with the county's best-ever figures on home soil -- seven for 56 -- as Notts were dismissed for 170.
Walker, who is out of contract at the end of the season, played in only three championship games last year and returned figures of two for 277.
However, with regular pace bowler Melvyn Betts injured, Boon overlooked four other young pacemen and called on Walker, who had a morning spell of four for 14 in 36 balls.
